name: Payment Transaction Map
principle: Phase 0.9 is behaviour-preserving. NO transaction boundary was added, removed, widened or narrowed. Every entry below describes the pre-existing boundary as it exists after the extraction.

transactions.name: Gateway order creation
sequence: 2. if a pending payment exists -> return it unchanged (is_existing = true)
transactions.concurrency_profile: Application-scoped, non-transactional. The pending-payment check and the insert are NOT atomic, so two concurrent create-order calls for the same booking can both pass step 1 and both insert. This is the pre-existing idempotency gap.
transactions.note: Step 2 IS the de facto order-reuse mechanism, but it is not a real idempotency guarantee because it is not transactional. No new idempotency system was introduced — that would change externally observable behaviour.

transactions.name: Payment signature verification and booking promotion
sequence: 2. gateway verifySignature(order_id, payment_id, signature) — LOCAL, no network
3. if invalid: update payment -> failed; update booking -> payment_failed; THROW (rolling back the writes)
4. if payment already paid: THROW 'Payment already processed'
5. if valid and unpaid: payment -> paid, paid_at set
transactions.concurrency_profile: No row lock is taken on the payment row. Two concurrent verify calls for the same order can both observe an unpaid payment and both proceed to step 5. The pre-existing duplicate guard (step 4) is a read-then-write check, not a serialisation mechanism.

rollback_behaviour.signature_failure: Payment and booking status updates are made and then an exception is thrown INSIDE the transaction, so the whole thing rolls back and the payment remains in its pre-verify state. This is a known, pre-existing oddity. Preserved verbatim.
rollback_behaviour.duplicate_paid: Transaction rolls back; no writes had been made.

transactions.note: verifySignature is a local cryptographic comparison, so keeping it inside the transaction carries no network-timeout risk. This is the one place where the in-transaction external call is genuinely benign.

transactions.name: Recorded refund (LIVE path)
transactions.external_call: PaymentGatewayInterface::refund() — REAL NETWORK I/O to Razorpay
sequence: 5. booking -> refunded ONLY when the refund is full
transactions.concurrency_profile: ARCHITECTURE RULE 4 VIOLATION (pre-existing). A real external network call is made while holding an open DB transaction. The row stays locked for the full duration of the gateway round-trip, and a gateway hang holds the transaction open for the same duration.
transactions.why_not_fixed: Moving the gateway call outside the transaction would change the failure semantics: currently a gateway failure rolls back cleanly and no refund row is written, and the gateway has NOT been debited. Moving the call out would risk a debited gateway with no local record on a subsequent DB failure. That is a redesign of financial failure semantics and is explicitly out of scope for an extraction phase.

transactions.name: Legacy gateway-only refund (DEAD PATH)
sequence: 1. gateway refund(payment_id, toPaise(amount) or null, notes)
NOTE: no Refund row, no PaymentLog
transactions.preserved_because: Deleting dead code is an observable change if any future route is wired to it, and the two refund paths diverge materially (refunds row + PaymentLog vs neither). Preserved for review in a dedicated cleanup phase.

transactions.name: Offline / direct payment recording
sequence: 2. Payment::create(...) with payment_mode, offline reference, verification_status = awaiting_verification
3. referral attribution when a referral code is attached
transactions.concurrency_profile: No lock. Concurrent offline recordings for the same booking will each insert a payment row.
transactions.note: The SIBLING path App\Http\Controllers\BookingController::markManualPayment() is a separate, divergent implementation and is NOT routed through this use case.

transactions.name: Admin payment approval with referral attribution
sequence: 1. payment -> completed, verification_status = verified, verified_by/verified_at set
transactions.concurrency_profile: The commission row lock is preserved verbatim through the repository move.
transactions.note: Only the service-locator call was replaced with constructor injection. The controller's own transaction boundary is unchanged.

pessimistic_lock_inventory.note: Only these three lock sites exist in the Payment/Financial subsystem. Payment and settlement paths contain NO pessimistic locks, before and after this phase.
explicitly_not_a_lock: Payment::firstOrFail() — plain SELECT, no FOR UPDATE
findPendingForBooking() — plain SELECT, no FOR UPDATE
